repo.description: The most widely used Python to C compiler
repo.name: cython

body:
In some cases, we generate inlined special casing code that matches a type slot and target it at certain known types, e.g. list/tuple iteration. We currently exclude subtypes because they can overwrite the base type's behaviour in arbitrary ways.

But it's easy and quick (in CPython) to compare the slot function pointer to that of the base type. If it has not been overwritten by the subclass, we can apply the same optimisation because we know that the behaviour has not changed.

It's not entirely clear that this is worth it and in which cases. Subtypes are rare, and having more guard conditions in place can slow down the really important (plain type) cases.

It should be worth doing when the initial overhead is small compared to the operation, e.g. when deciding whether to optimise a for-loop. For very short-running operations, it's probably less helpful.

comment_data.body:
I think it'll fail for the 3.9 Limited API (where `PyType_GetSlot` only supports heap-types, which does not include most builtin types and just reads some arbitrary memory where the type slots table should be).

The options are:
* Exclude on 3.9 Limited API.
* Use `PyType_TryGetSlot` (plus some extra logic about `NULL` slots since the functions will now return `NULL`)

I'd probably exclude personally, but either would work

   #define __Pyx_PyType_TryGetSubSlot(obj, sub, name, func_ctype) __Pyx_PyType_TryGetSlot(obj, name, func_ctype)
 #endif
 
+#if CYTHON_COMPILING_IN_CPYTHON && CYTHON_USE_TYPE_SLOTS

comment_data.body:
Actually, you wouldn't want `TryGetSlot` because that adds an extra "is heap type" check that would always fail. It'd be better to do a runtime version check only if you were going to go for the more complex option on 3.9.

I'd still just exclude it though personally

commit.message:
Allow builtin subtypes in a few optimisation cases.
If the slot that we optimise for has not been overwritten by the subclass, we can still apply the same optimisation.
Optimise list/tuple unpacking a little more.
Untangle list and tuple unpacking code.
Extend sequence unpacking benchmark to cover compile-time known tuples and lists.

Unroll sequence unpacking again.
According to the benchmarks, sequential statements seem visibly faster than indirect unpacking in a loop.
Include builtin subtypes in optimised object comparisons.
Include builtin subtypes in optimised dict iteration.
Include builtin subtypes in optimised set iteration.
Include builtin subtypes in optimised power operation.
Disable subtype optimisations outside of CPython.
Try to avoid going through PyNumber_Remainder() for formatting string subclasses into unicode strings.

title: Include subtypes of builtin types in some optimisations.
